summary.summary: Test Valley's 2025/26 treasury outturn is a clean report: all capital expenditure (£12.5m actual against an £18.0m forecast) was financed from existing resources and reserves, so no external borrowing arose from capital activity and the council reports full compliance with the gross-borrowing-vs-CFR prudential indicator. Investments were managed entirely in-house, growing from £90.3m to £108.7m over the year, and returned 4.62% against a 3.86% benchmark, beating the original budget for investment interest by £918,000 (and the February 2026 revised forecast by £92,000). The council deliberately kept cash balances thin and used reserves rather than external borrowing to fund capital spend, which the report frames as both cheaper (avoiding the borrowing/investment rate differential) and lower-risk (less counterparty exposure). The 4-page report circulated does not include the Annex containing the full prudential-indicator tables, so ratio-of-financing-costs and CFR figures themselves are not available to ground here.

signals.headline: No external borrowing in 2025/26, gross-borrowing-vs-CFR indicator complied with, and investment income beat original budget by £918,000 (£5.318m actual vs £4.4m budget)
signals.why: A council funding all its capital spend from reserves rather than debt, and outperforming its investment income budget, carries materially lower near-term financial risk than one drawing down reserves or borrowing to bridge gaps.

news_drafts.headline: Test Valley faces £170,000 building maintenance bill in first quarter as pressures mount
news_drafts.lead: Test Valley's building maintenance costs surged past budget by £169,571 in the first quarter to June 2026, driven by reactive repairs costing £180,976 against a profiled budget of £93,405 and planned maintenance overspending by £82,000. The council also faces a £73,000 pressure on temporary accommodation costs from increased demand. The overruns are partially contained by stronger-than-expected investment income, which exceeded budget by £118,000 as the council's investment portfolio delivered returns of 4.49 per cent against a benchmark of 3.85 per cent. The Cabinet approved continued budget monitoring across the year, signalling that quarterly reviews will track whether these early pressures persist.

findings.headline: Secretary of State approves stopping-up order for Western Avenue Riverside Park on 25 September 2026, removing key project risk and enabling construction contract commitment
findings.detail: Western Avenue Riverside Park required statutory stopping-up order for highway. Following public inquiry after objections to stopping-up application, Secretary of State for Transport gave approval in September 2026, with order taking effect 25 September 2026. Report states this removes "one of the main projects risks" and enables council to enter construction contract. Project scheduled for completion autumn 2028.
findings.matters: Removes regulatory risk blocking £12.65M project; enables capital spending to proceed; demonstrates project progress through development and approval stages.
findings.figures: £12.65M total project cost; autumn 2028 completion target; 20-month build period with fixed-price contractor commitment
findings.quote: In September 2026, the Secretary of State for Transport gave approval for the Order to be Made and this came into effect on 25th September 2026. Following the Stopping Up Order being Made by the Secretary of State for Transport, one of the main projects risks has been mitigated and enables the Council to enter into a contract for construction subject to approval of the required budget.

findings.headline: £8.85M of programme financing depends on land disposals with uncertain timing and values; further reliance on forecast CIL receipts and revenue budget performance
findings.detail: Financing table allocates £8.85M to capital receipts from land disposals discussed in confidential session. Report explicitly states timing and values are uncertain and could differ positively or negatively from forecast. Additional financing sources include £4.15M forecast CIL receipts through March 2029 and £7.9M forecast revenue contributions dependent on budget performance. S151 given flexibility to update financing forecast as crystallised figures emerge.
findings.matters: Multiple contingency points in financing plan; shortfall in any source could require reserve reductions or budget adjustments; peers and lenders need to understand funding risks and sensitivities.
findings.figures: £8.85M land disposals (contingent); £4.15M forecast CIL receipts; £7.9M forecast revenue contributions; £5M investment income uplift
findings.quote: In both cases, the timing and amount of the capital receipt is uncertain and it is possible that the final values could differ, positively or negatively, from the amounts built into this forecast.

findings.headline: Council forecasts £700,000 additional investment income in 2026/27 and £5M over three years as interest rates remain elevated
findings.detail: Higher interest rates set by Bank of England to control inflation have increased forecast investment income above baseline. First quarterly revenue budget monitoring for 2026/27 identifies £700k additional income above forecast. Medium-term financial forecast (2026/27 to 2028/29) forecasts further £5M from investments and budget variances beyond MTFS baseline, factored into capital programme funding.
findings.matters: Demonstrates positive financial impact of higher interest rates for cash-rich councils; programme funding assumptions depend on interest rates remaining elevated; reflects council's significant cash position and investment strategy.
findings.figures: £700,000 additional income forecast in 2026/27; £5M potential over 2026/27 to 2028/29 period
findings.quote: The first quarterly revenue budget monitoring report for 2026/27 has identified an increase in investment income that will be realised in this financial year, with potentially £700,000 above our forecast estimated to be achievable.

findings.headline: Construction input cost inflation at highest level since June 2022; Western Avenue and Vigo Park budgets increased for inflation and scope changes
findings.detail: Guardian article cited in report notes April 2026 construction input cost inflation (materials, energy, labour) at highest level since June 2022. Western Avenue Riverside Park budget revised to £12.65M post-tender from earlier estimate, with increase driven by inflation, contractor risk transfer over 20-month build, and site complexity including River Anton location and utility diversions. Vigo Park budget increased £500k for enhanced scope (recirculation system for splash park, Changing Places toilet, additional shading) and inflation impact.
findings.matters: Demonstrates ongoing construction cost pressure affecting capital programmes across sector; councils benchmarking against peers will see similar inflation impacts; risk of further overruns if design stages incomplete.
findings.figures: Western Avenue £12.65M total (approved £9.6M previously, approving £3.05M additional); Vigo Park £4M total (approved £3.5M previously, approving £0.5M additional)
findings.quote: input cost inflation – which accounts for expenses such as raw materials, energy and labour – rose last month to the highest level since June 2022

findings.headline: Council commits £41.53M from revenue and capital reserves to fund capital programme
findings.detail: Programme will draw £29.42M from revenue reserves (supplementing current balance with forecast future contributions) and £9.368M from capital reserves. Combined revenue reserve balance was £27.8M at 31 March 2026, with £12.1M already committed. S151 Officer confirms reserves are adequate and will not jeopardise future budget setting.
findings.matters: Large one-time reserve draw on concentrated funding source; programme depends on future revenue generation and investment income forecasts; materially affects long-term investment income position; peers and lenders assess reserve sustainability.
findings.figures: £41.53M total draw (£29.42M revenue + £9.368M capital); combined reserve balance £27.8M; prior commitments £12.1M; forecast future revenue contributions £7.9M over 2026/27 to 2028/29
findings.quote: the Director of Finance & Revenues, who is the Council's S151 Officer, confirms that the use of reserves as set out in the report will not jeopardise future years' budget setting or the ongoing delivery of services.

daily_post.headline: Investment income is exceeding budget by £118,000, driven by strong portfolio returns.
daily_post.lead: Investment income outperformance indicates effective cash management in an elevated interest rate environment. However, it is contingent on the council maintaining adequate cash balances and interest rates remaining elevated, both of which may not be…
